prompt:
Goal: Create a charming pixel-art character sheet of a fluffy cream kitten as a cute virtual companion, arranged like a retro game asset preview.

Canvas: Horizontal 3:2 composition on a warm off-white paper background with a faint square grid, subtle beige texture, and thin pale divider lines near the top and bottom.

Layout: Show exactly 6 separate kitten sprites in a clean 3-column by 2-row grid with generous spacing. Add tiny monospaced gray interface text across the top: “CAT · COMPANION · GOOD BOY” on the left, a long thin horizontal line through the middle, and “MEOW.EXE RUNNING ..” on the right. Add bottom text: “SMALL CAT · BIG HAPPINESS” on the left, a thin line across the center, and “EST. 2024” on the right.

Subject details: The kitten is extremely fluffy, cream-white with soft beige shading, round oversized dark gray eyes, small pink nose, triangular ears with pink inner ears, tiny paws, plush tail, and a slightly dark pixel-outline. Use hand-painted pixel art with soft dithering and a cozy pastel palette.

Exactly 6 poses and labels:
1. Top left: sitting front-facing kitten, a small blue pixel heart floating to its right, label “>_ hello”.
2. Top center: kitten lying stretched horizontally with tail to the left and head to the right, two tiny blue sparkle icons above, label “>_ chill”.
3. Top right: sitting front-facing kitten looking curious, three small blue motion marks to its right, label “>_ curious”.
4. Bottom left: kitten curled up sleeping with eyes closed, blue “Z z” symbols above, label “>_ sleep”.
5. Bottom center: small front-facing kitten bust/sitting pose with a speech bubble containing a blue heart to its right, label “>_ meow”.
6. Bottom right: kitten viewed from behind, fluffy tail curled left, small blue motion marks to its right, label “>_ thinking”.

Visual style: Nostalgic cozy pixel art, soft hand-drawn shading, muted cream, gray, beige, pink, and powder-blue accents; all labels in tiny gray terminal-style monospaced text.

Constraints: Keep the image uncluttered, no photorealism, no extra kittens, no additional labels beyond the specified interface text and six pose labels, no watermark.
